requirements.verifier_assertion: The v3 proto file must exist at /app/proto/v3/generate.proto and contain the exact `package generate.v3;` declaration (test_outputs.py L349-353).

The v3 proto must retain `service TextGenerationService` and every RPC (Info, ServiceDiscovery, ClearCache, FilterBatch, Warmup, Prefill, Decode, Health) exactly as v2, with message definitions identical for now (test_outputs.py L355-358).

The text-generation-client crate must expose `text_generation_client::v2` and `text_generation_client::v3` modules, each re-exporting Client, ShardedClient, and that version's proto types Batch/CachedBatch/Request/NextTokenChooserParameters/StoppingCriteriaParameters/Generation/GrammarType (test_outputs.py L384, L391-409 compile probe).

The client crate root must expose a `ShardInfo` struct with fields requires_padding, dtype, device_type, window_size, speculate, converted from each version's InfoResponse (test_outputs.py L393-399 default-construct check).

The client crate root must expose an async `Health` trait with `device_health` and `model_health` methods, implemented by both v2::ShardedClient and v3::ShardedClient (test_outputs.py L384-390 compile probe).

Router-side inference code (health checks, queueing, batching) moves into an `infer` module split by protocol version; queueing/batching is abstracted behind a `Scheduler` trait taking validated requests plus concurrency permits and returning a streaming response channel.
The v2 Scheduler implementation must keep the existing behavior completely unchanged — v2 client plus existing queue logic (test_outputs.py L521-525 v2 stack behavior identical).

The v3 Scheduler implementation must go through the v3 client and convert validated request parameters into v3 proto types at the queue boundary, including the JSON/Regex enum mapping for grammar; batching, concatenation, stop conditions stay consistent (test_outputs.py L453-459 v3 stack behavior).

At startup the router tries v3 first against --master-shard-uds-path; on success it logs `Using scheduler V3` at info level; on failure it falls back to v2 and logs `Using scheduler V2`. Log literals must be exact (test_outputs.py L443, L511).
The same router binary must handle either shard generation with no extra configuration — the protocol version is auto-detected at startup, not a new CLI flag or env var.
The scattered initialization sequence in main (connect to shards, clear the cache, fetch shard info, warmup) moves into the server startup flow.

When the shard reports a max_batch_total_tokens limit via warmup, use the reported value; warn if --max-batch-total-tokens is also passed; exit with an error when --max-total-tokens exceeds the shard-reported limit (test_outputs.py L497-502 /info returns 4096; L552-556 non-zero exit within 90s).
When the shard does not report a warmup cap, fall back to max(16000, --max-total-tokens, --max-batch-prefill-tokens); `/info` reports 16000 on v2 shard with no cap (test_outputs.py L531-532).
`/health` semantics are unchanged: use the liveness probe (model_health) until there is a successful generation record, then switch to the lightweight device_health (test_outputs.py L494 200).

Existing HTTP API semantics (/generate, /generate_stream, /health, /info, /tokenize, etc.) must not change; behavior on old v2 shards must be exactly the same as today (test_outputs.py L521-532 v2 stack matches contract).

The existing router and client unit tests must keep passing; every crate in the workspace must pass `cargo build` (test_outputs.py L297-300 cargo build --workspace; L430-433 cargo test router+client).
